clips.send: Someone grinding 60-hour weeks at a new business sends this to a friend ready to quit, proof that every plane needs full throttle before it ever reaches cruising altitude.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says making money works exactly like flying a plane.

The pilot takes his foot off the brake and the plane goes from standing still to barreling down the runway, picking up speed and speed, full throttle, flaps down, until it finally lifts off the ground.

Even after liftoff he stays full throttle, climbing, climbing, climbing.

Only once he reaches cruising altitude does he pull back on the throttle and flip on autopilot.

That's the part everyone skips: wanting the autopilot stage while they're still standing at the end of the runway.

Are you still building power, or are you trying to cruise before you've even taken off?

clips.send: A small business owner who can't afford a $100,000 copywriter sends this to a friend starting an online store, proof that an AI system can now get close to that same result for free.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says one of his students built something that should scare every $100,000-a-project copywriter.

The guy learned copywriting from Kevin and others, then built an AI system that writes sales copy from nothing more than a few answered questions.

He ran it head to head against real, paid, professional copywriters in A/B tests. Kevin's words: it did as good, and in some cases better.

Kevin charges people $100,000 plus a cut of sales to write copy personally. This system gets close to that same result for free.

Would you still pay six figures for copy if a few typed answers got you most of the way there?
